briefing.summary: Dive to the battleship Bismarck on the flank of an extinct seamount. Scan the upright main hull and the detached gun turrets higher on the slope, then inspect the hull for battle damage.
facts: Bismarck sank on 27 May 1941 after a pursuit by the Royal Navy. Robert Ballard’s team found the wreck in June 1989.
The hull rests upright on a seamount slope. Its stern broke away and the four main gun turrets fell out during the sinking.
The dive follows a roughly 4,220 m terrain slope. Published surveys place the real wreck at about 4,790 m; the Journal explains the mapping gap.
With a surface start, head southwest from the starting point and descend toward the hull.
hazards: Sunlight fades with depth; use your lights to read the deeper terrain.
Crushing pressure: about 420 atmospheres on this route. Your Class C hull is rated beyond it.
Steep, unstable seamount flank terrain near the wreck.
Unexploded ordnance may remain aboard. Keep a respectful distance and do not touch anything.
briefing.memorial_note: Bismarck is a war grave. About 2,100 crew died when she sank. Explore with care: observe, photograph and leave the wreck undisturbed.

objectives.title: Scan the main hull
objectives.hint: Find the upright hull on the seamount's southeastern flank, around 4,210 m.

objectives.title: Survey the detached turrets
objectives.hint: Head east and upslope from the hull to the turrets, around 4,120 m.

objectives.title: Inspect the battle damage
objectives.hint: Inspect the battle-damage marker near the main hull, around 4,210 m.
